discussion_comments.comment_body: Valid, fixed. A link whose target is a directory already on the current copy chain, or an ancestor of one (`.`, `..`, a sibling that links back), is now skipped and listed in `skippedPaths` instead of being expanded again, and the number of linked-directory expansions is capped (`MAX_LINK_EXPANSIONS`). Covered by "skips links that loop back into a directory being copied": twenty links to `.` plus one to `..` finish in well under a second with only the real content copied.

Intentional tradeoff. A cut-off stream whose last 2k non-whitespace chars are pure 0/1 is rare, and it fails with a clear error rather than stopping silently. Loosening the check to allow it would weaken detection of the real repetition-loop case, so leaving it as is.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
The 32k floor is intentional following review feedback: applying 30% directly lowered existing output allowances and could cause more truncation and retries.
Compared with main, an 8k model still receives an 8k cap, and a 64k model still receives 32k. Only sufficiently large models receive an increase. For example, 128k → 38,400. The existing model and context clamps remain in place.
The PR description still described the earlier proportional reduction; I’ve corrected it. Using the fraction directly would reintroduce the issue identified in the earlier review, so I believe this P1 can be closed.
